question: Does the frozen D2b activity-written RBS produce activity-dependent adaptation with recovery under a repeated-pulse paradigm?

terminology.note: fatigue-like may be used post hoc as phenomenological description only; implemented state is effective K-associated recovery driven by activity history

scientific_scope.included: D3 repeated-pulse adaptation/recovery phenotype specification only
scientific_scope.excluded: D3 implementation, HDP, geometry, delays, fields, SSA, oddball, habituation, microscopic fatigue mechanism claims

paradigm.display: baseline -> repeated stimulation -> recovery interval -> rechallenge

phases.role: pre-stimulus reference epoch for hidden states and spontaneous activity
adaptation induction; no stimulus parameter changes across repetitions
prospective recovery duration sweep; holds all else fixed

phases.drive: single pulse identical to train pulses
phases.role: recovery readout; same amplitude, duration, and analysis window as train pulses

pulse_train.note: fixed amplitude, duration, and ISI across all repetitions and rechallenge

timing.derivation_note: train ends at 100 + (m-1)*isi + duration = 100 + 300 + 40 = 440 ms; total duration accommodates longest recovery plus rechallenge and post window

recovery_intervals.selection_rule: prospective from D2b timescales tau_A=25 ms, tau_K=100 ms; not tuned from spike responses

levels.rationale: 2 * tau_A; partial H_A decay, minimal H_K restoration
2.5 * tau_K; substantial H_K restoration toward reference

recovery_intervals.mechanistic_prediction: T_recovery up => H_K(T_rechallenge) -> 1 and, if H_K mediates adaptation, R_rechallenge -> R_early

primary.definition: spike count in fixed post-stimulus window following pulse j onset

secondary.definition: voltage integral over the same post-stimulus window as R_j
latency to first spike in the post-stimulus window; undefined if zero spikes

R_early.definition: mean of R_j over early pulse indices

R_late.definition: mean of R_j over late pulse indices

interpretation.negative: facilitation; must be retained, not converted to failure metadata

recovery_index.domain: defined only when denominator R_early - R_late != 0

interpretation.note: perfect recovery not required; secondary metric/classification

recovery_index.classification_role: secondary; not required for initial ADAPTATION classification

null_hierarchy.display: N0 classical | N1 static H_K=1 | N2 kappa_AK=0 (D2a) | D full D2b

arms.label: kappa_AK = 0 (D2a dynamics only)
arms.note: H_A may evolve from local spikes but does not write H_K

primary_contrast.statement: both include dynamic H_K restoration; only D allows activity history to write H_K

hidden_state_mechanism_checks.scope: D arm and full D2b hidden-state traces; not sufficient for adaptation classification alone

during_repeated_stimulation.statement: mean H_A over late train pulses > mean H_A over baseline epoch
mean H_K over late train pulses > 1 (requires kappa_AK > 0)

during_recovery.statement: H_A -> 0 toward reference during recovery interval
H_K -> 1 toward reference during recovery interval

hidden_state_mechanism_checks.informative_null_outcome: mechanism checks pass but A_adapt <= 0 => reduced coupling does not produce desired adaptation phenotype under frozen paradigm; not a D2b failure

ADAPTATION.note: phenotype requires both observable and mechanism condition on D arm

UNRESOLVED.requires: signal quality insufficient to define meaningful adaptation index
UNRESOLVED.example: R_early too sparse; do not treat silence as adaptation

interpretation_rules: NO_ADAPTATION is a valid scientific outcome, not a protocol failure
mechanism_ok with NO_ADAPTATION means this reduced K-associated coupling does not yield adaptation under the frozen paradigm
D2b state-space contract is not retroactively invalidated by NO_ADAPTATION
negative A_adapt indicates facilitation and must be reported
UNRESOLVED must be reported when early response is too sparse
recovery classification is secondary to adaptation classification
do not use fatigue as formal microscopic mechanism in D3 receipts
